paper_title: AgentProofBench: Benchmarking Reusable Verifiers for Web Agents

sections.title: Abstract
sections.content: Reusable Web-agent verification requires a rule to follow changing requirements and support subsequent execution. We introduce AgentProofBench, which connects paired tests of a frozen acceptance rule to execution from identical saved openings. The resource spans 97 tasks, 79 families, and four Web services. Experiments with DeepSeek Flash/Pro establish two linked measurements. Across 48 families, complete-panel and decision-replay tests retain 82/96 Flash and 79/96 Pro source programs; paired reuse-rebuild BA intervals are [-5.47, 1.57] and [-10.16, 0.00] percentage points. Across 22 execution families, deployment-state panel correctness separates program assignments whose two saved openings are both delivered correctly: 32/33 assignments with error-free panels, versus 1/11 with panel errors. All reference-defined program-gate regressions and withheld deliveries occur in the latter group. Neutral continuation attains the highest correct delivery under the tested generic feedback, providing a concrete baseline for measuring the value added by a gate. Released instructions, states, programs, reference rules, and trajectories connect each test failure to its execution consequences. AgentProofBench makes reusable verification assessable at both the requirement and policy levels.

sections.title:
1 INTRODUCTION
Reusable acceptance checks can make Web-agent operation fast and
inspectable. A program can encode the conditions for completing a
task, inspect the relevant business state, and issue the same explicit
checks on subsequent executions. The central challenge is that the
public instruction can stay fixed while the required work changes.
The current owner of a name, the files belonging to a collection,
or the value that must be preserved comes from the initial state of
each execution. A verifier that remembers an earlier answer can
produce a convincing decision for the wrong requirement.
sections.content: The decision also becomes part of the agents environment. Rejection can trigger further edits, and acceptance can release the resulting state. Evaluating reusable verifier therefore requires link between the conditions its tests exercise and the outcomes of 1 the policy that consumes its decisions. Matched continuation histories make that link observable: the same completed work can be preserved, changed, or withheld under different stopping policies. Existing Web-agent environments establish executable task evaluation [15, 20, 22, 23, 31]. Work on automatic assessment and generated verifiers demonstrates the importance of evidence and acceptance of valid alternatives [8, 16, 24]. Reusable execution policies further show the value of experience across workflow instances [19]. These advances motivate an evaluation that connects three properties of an acceptance rule. It must recognize the permitted terminal outcomes, recover the requirements of changed initial state, and support effective continuation and delivery decisions. We introduce AgentProofBench around this connection. An acceptance program is executable code that judges task completion through ordinary before/after APIs. reuse contract fixes the public instruction and evidence permissions while initial business data vary. Matched terminal outcomes make the consequences of this variation observable. Shared actor openings then connect the same verifier to the actions taken after its decision. Every measurement is linked to versioned reference predicates, program source, API evidence, and reconstructable business state. The benchmark provides three contributions. paired reuse test that holds the public instruction and generated program fixed while changing its required initialstate bindings. Complete outcome panels and replayed decisions measure complementary obligations. An execution-validity test linking deployment-state panel correctness to matched policy outcomes. The 22-family study preserves 44 program assignments, two openings per assignment, and 352 policy outcomes. An executable resource with 97 tasks across four Web services, including versioned reference rules, legal alternatives, reconstructable states, programs, and action histories. The central empirical result is the connection between tests and execution. Programs with error-free deployment-state panels correctly deliver both saved openings in 32 of 33 assignments, compared with one of eleven assignments whose panels contain errors. The paired reuse study explains which requirements those panels exercise; replay witnesses expose additional errors in three source programs. Fixed-instance acceptance and cost profiles then describe the operating tradeoffs of the same verification interface. The reported generator, judge, and actor results use DeepSeek Flash/Pro with thinking disabled.

sections.title: 2 RELATED WORK
sections.content: Executable evaluation and generated verifiers. WebArena, OSWorld, 𝜏-bench, and AppWorld provide executable task environments [20, 22, 23, 31]. Agent-Diff supplies the enterprise-service replicas used here [15]; OpenComputer and WorkForge develop verifiable software worlds and workspace criteria [21, 27]. The testoracle literature establishes the broader problem of trustworthy acceptance rules [1]. CodeT and Eureka generate executable tests or rewards [3, 9], while SpecGuardBench and WebGrader evaluate generated validation code [2, 30]. Rules to Tools supplies callable implementations of scientific requirements for program repair [12]. VerifierBench tests executable verifier generation across six agent Ning et al. benchmarks, including legal alternatives, ordinary errors, and attacks [24]. AgentProofBench extends the measurement target to matched initial-state requirements and the subsequent execution controlled by verifier decisions. Evidence-based judgment. Agent-as-a-Judge, AJ-Bench, and AgentRewardBench study assessment from environment and trajectory evidence [8, 18, 32]. Universal Verifier develops criterionbased computer-use assessment [16]; Sauron gathers state and trace evidence for its judgments [17]. VAGEN and VeriHarness study agentic verification and structured evidence collection [4, 26]. LLM-as-a-Verifier examines continuous scores, repeated evaluation, and criterion decomposition [7]. Our fresh API judgments share the frozen states and ordinary evidence permissions of the executable programs, enabling direct comparison of valid acceptance, failure rejection, and repeated-use cost. Reuse and verification during execution. SkillLearnBench evaluates learned artifacts across task instances [29]. ControlScope studies how workflow-revision permissions shape subsequent execution [10]. Revision or Re-Solving uses matched conditions to separate sources of second-pass gains [11]. CLIFT reuses frozen self-verification bank for training and trajectory selection [28]. Neuro-Symbolic Computer Use learns reusable execution policies under initial-state and parameter variation, with verification-guided continuation [19]. SPLIT allocates computation across sampling and imperfect verification, and verifier hardening combines adversarial improvement with protection of valid solutions [6, 25]. Enterprise-agent studies connect verification, model roles, and task completion [5]. The Implementation Lottery compares reuse of selected program with fresh implementations of its mechanism [14]. DCP compares truthful and neutral feedback from shared checkpoints in scientific-research audits [13]. Figure 2 connects paired verifier tests with execution from shared histories.

sections.title:
3.2 Outcome coverage and reference semantics
Three linked studies address acceptance, reuse, and execution. The
acceptance resource contains 97 tasks from 79 families, with 20
family-disjoint development tasks. Its 556-state natural panel in-
cludes 452 successes and 104 failures, sampled by reference class
with at most six states per task. The reuse study evaluates 576
programs on 558 terminal states from 48 families. The execution
study compares policies on 88 saved openings from 22 families.
Appendix A records the natural-state selection flow and the three
post-inspection task exclusions.
sections.content: Four outcome panels separate common acceptance demands (Figure 7). Natural outcomes measure ordinary agent endings. Nativeprefix pairs use service actions to connect complete execution to an earlier incomplete state. Typed faults alter successful anchor through service APIs, allowing the violated requirement to be identified. Legal alternatives change behavior that the public instruction permits. Successful anchors and failed states jointly test valid acceptance and failure rejection. Reference predicates cover identities, values, collections, and relationships. Versioned selectors recover the required objects from each before state. Native-state and ordinary-API evaluation share the predicates and check restoration and evidence accessibility. Scores measure conformity to this explicit reference contract. Appendix retains the original and explicit-preservation label views. separate GPT-6 Astra LLM-as-a-judge audit reviews 195 states across 62 tasks, with reference verdicts withheld during initial judgment. It agrees with 191 of 192 resolved labels (99.5%); three cases are indeterminate. The audit corroborates all 48 requirement changes, rejects all 48 failed replays, and confirms both deliveredregression pairs (Appendix A). The preservation task linear_52 illustrates the contract. Its instruction assigns Plot B3 to Rashida and requires its initial status to survive. The source state has status Active; the related state has Dormant. The reference resolves Plot B3 from the current before state, checks the requested assignee, and compares its before/after status identifiers. correct related outcome therefore keeps Dormant. The instructions other clauses create tracker issue and update Plots A7 and C1. They supply additional matched outcomes while the B3 change isolates the state-dependent preservation requirement. The complete instruction and predicates appear in Appendix A.

sections.title:
3.3 Matched initial-state reuse
The matched study, P1, selects one task from each of 48 original fam-
ilies, comprising 18 Linear, 10 Slack, 19 Box, and one Calendar task.
Every family contributes one related initial-state transformation.
Each public instruction has three initial conditions. Source is the
construction state. Background changes data outside the requested
work. Related changes a required entity binding, initial value, col-
lection, or preservation condition. An entity binding identifies the
object denoted by a public name; a preservation condition requires
an initial value to survive execution.
sections.content: Qualification establishes four properties before prediction. The changed requirement follows the public instruction, service actions construct the states, native and API references agree on matched outcomes, and replaying source-valid decision becomes invalid under the related condition. This last execution is source-decision witness. It tests the acceptance rule against an earlier valid business decision whose required target or value has changed. The witness gives initial-state variation direct semantic test. If the same earlier decision remains valid, program could succeed by retaining its source answer. qualified witness requires the verifier to resolve new condition from the current before state. This separates state-dependent acceptance from incidental differences in snapshot and makes the changed obligation inspectable in the reference and API trace. Each initial condition contains complete result, distinct legal alternative where available, and two changed failures. Fault recipes and their roles remain matched across conditions; the current before state supplies identifiers and required values. Forty-two tasks have two valid outcomes per condition, and six have one. The 144 initial states support 558 main terminal states, comprising 270 valid and 288 failed entries. Witness pairs add one source-valid and one related-invalid decision per task, with their own scoring support. DeepSeek Flash and Pro, both with thinking disabled, each generate two source programs and two rebuilt programs at each target condition, producing 576 frozen artifacts. Construction and 3 fresh online API assessment, denoted API12, allow twelve model turns. Programs can read and debug against their construction state. Source programs run on all three conditions, while target rebuilds are compared at their own construction target. Two independent API12 judgments per model and terminal state give 2,232 online observations. The full three-construction by three-assessment matrix additionally measures reverse transfer.

sections.title:
3.4 Verification during continued execution
The execution study, P2, uses 22 families with a native completion
trace containing at least two mutating operations. One Flash and
one Pro actor per task generate 44 trajectories from related initial
states. Every trajectory supplies a natural ending and a closed
checkpoint, saved after its first complete tool round containing a
mutating request. Each of the 88 openings preserves the original
initial state, current business state, and complete interaction history.
Four policies branch from each opening. Actor stop delivers on
the actor’s final reply. Its non-final checkpoint outcome is a me-
chanical no-delivery reference. Fixed continue allows two neutral
continuation phases and delivers on a final reply after phase two.
Program gate uses a source-built Pro program, assigned by a fixed
parity rule per task and actor independently of source quality. On-
line gate uses fresh Pro API12 judgments. Both gates deliver on Pass
and otherwise permit at most two continuations. The two cohorts
retain the same assigned program.
sections.content: The neutral message asks the actor to finish the original request while preserving completed work. Gate feedback prepends statement of nonacceptance and carries no program checks or entity identifiers. Thus each branch evaluates complete feedbackand-stopping policy; Appendix gives the exact messages. An eight-family development study selected this design before formal actor prediction. Each actor phase allows 20 model turns and 100 business operations, with USD 1 observed-cost stop and 900second deadline. Unresolved usage stops further work. Executed writes persist when delivery is withheld.

4 RESULTS
4.1 Joint tests of initial-state reuse
The paired study measures whether an acceptance rule follows a
changed requirement while its instruction and code remain fixed.
Source programs obtain related-state BA of 93.23% for Flash and
90.36% for Pro (Table 1). Reuse-minus-rebuild estimates are -1.56
points with interval [-5.47, 1.57] and -4.95 with [-10.16, 0.00]. Both
prespecified intervals include equal mean BA; the Pro range ex-
tends to −10.16 points. The background control produces identical
verdicts under the tested unrelated edits.
sections.content: Complete main-panel correctness changes from 89/96 to 83/96 source programs for Flash and from 83/96 to 81/96 for Pro. Conditional on fully correct source panel, the retained counts are 83/89 and 80/83, spanning 45 and 46 source-qualified families. Six Flash and three Pro programs acquire an error across three families per model; one initially incorrect Pro program becomes correct on the related panel. Figure 3 keeps the full 96-program denominator visible. The added witness probes an earlier valid decision at its changed requirement. Source programs accept 92/96 valid source witnesses for Flash and 89/96 for Pro. After the related change, they falsely accept 6/96 and 5/96 replays, while related rebuilds accept 5/96 and 2/96. Pro source programs also give two Unknown and two Error verdicts on related witnesses. Joint correctness requires resolved, correct verdict on both the main panel and its witness. Its resulting counts are 82/96 Flash and 79/96 Pro source programs, compared with 82/96 and 86/96 rebuilds (Figure 3). Rebuilt main panels are completely correct for 85/96 Flash and 87/96 Pro programs. Within the source-joint-qualified subsets, related joint correctness is 82/89 and 78/83. sections.title:
4.2 Panel correctness and execution outcomes
Deployment-state tests are strongly associated with the recorded
execution outcomes. Of 33 assigned programs with error-free re-
lated panels, 32 correctly deliver both their natural ending and
checkpoint. Of eleven assignments with a panel error, one cor-
rectly delivers both openings (Figure 4). At the opening level the
corresponding counts are 64/66 and 2/22. The assignment is the
summary unit: its two openings share one trajectory and have iden-
tical correct-versus-incorrect/withheld dispositions in this study.
The 44 assignments come from 22 task families. The associated
correct-delivery difference is 87.9 percentage points, with a point-
wise family-cluster interval of [68.8, 100.0].

4.3 Acceptance profiles on shared outcomes
Fixed-instance tests describe the operating profile that accom-
panies reuse and execution. The restrictive-acceptance pattern
is consistent with VerifierBench [24]: generated programs reject
invalid outcomes more reliably than they accept valid alterna-
tives. Here B4/B12 denote four-/twelve-call program construction,
and API12/JSON12 denote twelve-call online judgments with
ordinary/structured output. The following comparisons use Flash.
The collection comparison uses identical before/after states and
the same explicit-condition reference labels: 99 failed states and
36 successful anchors across 36 tasks and 29 families, with two
observations per method. B12 false acceptance is 3.5% versus 31.7%
for API12, a paired task-mean difference of −28.2 points (95% family-
bootstrap interval [−40.7, −16.7]). Valid-anchor acceptance is 77.8%
versus 98.6%. Figure 5 preserves both outcomes and the distributions
behind each mean.

sections.title:
4.4 Construction cost and the reuse horizon
Repeated use separates the fixed cost of creating a program from
the cost of invoking it. The matched P1 fee comparison contains
80 Flash units from 43 families and 83 Pro units from 44 families,
with known charges for all three constructions and their online
judgments. Median source construction costs are USD 0.0173/0.0765.
A fresh online pass over the corresponding 9- or 12-state panel costs
USD 0.0188/0.0980. Rounding each construction-to-mean-online-
fee ratio upward gives median API-fee break-even horizons of
twelve assessments for Flash and ten for Pro, with ranges 2–29 and
2–36.
sections.content: For P2, let 𝐶 be the assigned construction fee and 𝑐 the observed actor-prefix and branch cost. The amortized fee at 𝑘 uses is 𝑐 + 𝐶/𝑘, and warm operation costs 𝑐. Figure 6 shows the resulting deployment views next to online gating and neutral continuation. At ten uses, Flash program-gate means are USD 0.0195 for natural endings and USD 0.0189 for checkpoints. Their cold means are USD 0.1396 and USD 0.1390. Pros corresponding ten-use means are USD 0.0509 and USD 0.0478. Construction and ongoing execution thus have distinct roles in the cost comparison. The reuse horizon complements the acceptance and delivery profiles. low-cost invocation is useful when its rule covers the required outcomes, and highly discriminative judge can justify repeated inference where valid completions vary. The observed policy branches further show that construction amortization and downstream correctness are separate measurements. The released ledger counts each request once; policy views allocate the shared prefix and assigned construction explicitly. The companion retains every cold, warm, and amortized policy record.

sections.title:
5 USING THE BENCHMARK
AgentProofBench supports three concrete evaluation workflows. A
verifier generator can be tested on the same natural endings, legal
alternatives, and typed failures to establish its acceptance profile.
Its frozen outputs can then be evaluated under matched initial-state
requirements using both complete-panel and joint witness correct-
ness. Finally, the recorded actor openings support comparison of
the policies that consume these decisions, measuring completed
work, persistent mutations, and delivered state separately.
sections.content: The resource connects these workflows through stable task, family, program, and state identities. Each false acceptance links to violated reference condition; each transfer error links to source program and target rebuild; each execution outcome links to the gate decision and subsequent requests. generator improvement can therefore be assessed against the changed requirement it should recover and the policy outcome it should support. The companions Evidence Index provides the acceptance, reuse, and execution entry points. Canonical snapshots and exact row deltas reconstruct the saved states. The verify(task, before, after) interface evaluates frozen programs without model calls. Ning et al.

sections.title:
6 CONCLUSION
AgentProofBench connects the two requirements of reusable
Web-agent verification: recovering the current task obligation and
supporting subsequent execution. Paired initial states and replay
witnesses test the first; shared actor histories and program-level
outcome links test the second. In the DeepSeek Flash/Pro study,
deployment-state panel correctness identifies 32/33 assignments
whose two openings are delivered correctly, compared with 1/11
assignments containing panel errors. Neutral continuation anchors
the measurement of gate value, while acceptance profiles and
amortized costs describe operating choices. The released 97-task re-
source makes this chain reproducible, from a changed requirement
to a tested rule and its observed execution consequences.
